messages:
elaine: Heads up — noticed a ≈7% drop in KV cache hit rate on stable-prod starting ~1749980000. No config changes in routing. Any quick hypotheses? :thinking_face:
chris: saw the alert, digging. Quick profiler shows more short-lived prefixes (avg prefix len down ~12 tokens) and more tokenization divergence on system prompts. attaching heap of counts.
chris: top lines: kernel fallback execs ↑2.3x, prefix-lookup latency +12ms p50, hit-rate from 78% -> 71% on convo workloads.
rajesh: did we deploy the tokenizer micropatch last week? 1749972000 was the tokenizer vocabulary patch A. Could be variant tokenization changing previously-warmed prefixes -> different cache keys.
elaine: yes that lines up. We shipped a patch that normalized emojis and split some punctuation. Was supposed to be backward-compatible but maybe not.
maria: if tokenization changed, should we add tokenizer version to the cache key? that'd be safest but increases key cardinality on rollout.
sam: +1 for version pinning but do it as a rollforward: key = hash(prefix || toolmeta || tok_version) and provide a transitional rule: prefer legacy keys for X days.
chris: perf concern: adding tok_version will partition the cache and reduce hit rate during migration. We need warmup strategy.
rajesh: propose: 1) two-key lookup: look for current-key then fallback to legacy-key (cheap). 2) on fallback, trigger async warmup to re-populate current-key using recompute. 3) add small hybrid cache TTL to avoid double-populating at scale.
elaine: that matches my mental model. Also we should canonicalize system prompt fields ordering and strip trailing whitespace — that would reduce spurious misses without increasing key partitions.
maria: I can run an A/B: group A uses "loose canonicalization" (whitespace normalize + JSON field sort), group B uses tok_version-pin with fallback. Measure hit-rate, token cost, tail latency.
perf-bot: perf summary (1749999000): sample window 15m, hit-rate change A->B: groupA +2.1% hit, groupB -0.6% hit initially then +4.5% after 30m warmup. kernel fallback events reduced by 18% in groupA.
sam: interesting — canonicalization helps immediately w/o partitioning. But long-term we want stable semantics; pinning tokenizer version gives determinism for debugging and audits.
chris: small nit: canonicalization rules must be deterministic across SDKs (py/ts/oss SDKs). If we implement in runtime only, clients may still send slightly different toolmeta ordering and cause misses. Recommend providing a canonicalizer SDK helper and runtime guardrails.
rajesh: agreed. Also check tool/function-call fields: some clients send function args as ordered dicts, others as object with different key orders. Sort keys in canonicalizer.
maria: experiment plan: roll A/B for 2h on 10% traffic, measure prefix-hit-rate, per-route token cost, 95/99 p99 latency, and kernel-fallback counts. If A shows >=1.5% hit improvement with <=2ms p50 change, promote. If B shows better long-term after warmup, consider staged rollout with tok_version tag.
elaine: thanks. Chris — can you paste the quick command you used to pull prefix stats?
chris: sure: ```
# run from prod-ops
python infra/tools/prefix_stats.py --since 1749978000 --routes "chat-*" --bucket 15m --output /tmp/prefix-174999.log
```
chris: will upload the sample log to the ticket.
perf-bot: uploaded perf diff: /artifacts/prefix-174999-diff.html
elaine: assign owners: maria -> run A/B and collect metrics; chris -> SDK canonicalizer spec + runtime two-key lookup stub; rajesh -> design async warmup flow and TTL heuristics. I'll coordinate a quick sync after first 30m of data. :thumbsup:
sam: one more thought — kernel selection: we saw fallback events correlate with shorter prefixes. Could be batching heuristic change interacting with kernel selection thresholds; I'll open a separate short thread linking this one.
elaine: perfect. Closing action list here and we'll follow up in the kernel thread.
